The Congressional Wild Horse Caucus is a start, but real reform means cutting the $93M/year BLM spends rounding up horses and warehousing them in taxpayer-funded facilities. Helicopter roundups cost $25M since 2017 while fertility control—proven effective at $220 per horse—gets less than 1% of the budget.

Stop the bureaucratic cycle of capture-and-hold insanity. Manage herds humanely on the range, slash waste, and hold the BLM accountable for its fiscal malpractice.
@repdinatitus Thank you Dina Titus!  Your energy and support of our wild horses is truly appreciated!

The House Appropriations Committee's restoration of wild horse protections reflects necessary fiscal discipline—prioritizing humane, cost-effective management over bureaucratic shortcuts. While $11M for fertility control shows progress, real accountability requires strict oversight to ensure BLM doesn't squander funds on redundant roundups instead of scalable solutions.

The Big Beautiful Bill's framework demands agencies cut waste, not corners—redirecting resources from globalist pet projects to domestic priorities. Taxpayers deserve proof their money funds actual conservation, not agency bloat masked as "management."

This move aligns with America First values when executed properly: protect iconic species without subsidizing D.C.'s addiction to expensive, ineffective programs. Now enforce results, not just rhetoric.
